admission.content: Implement alpha() int returning 42 instead of 0. Only alpha.go and alpha_test.go may change. RED: add exactly one ordinary Go unit test named TestAlpha in alpha_test.go; if alpha()!=42 call t.Fatal("got 0 want 42"). Do not change production code until implement stage. Preserve all test bytes in implementation. Use package sample, standard gofmt tabs and blank lines. Report actual complete test source in source fields. No other functions, dependencies, commands, external effects or files are needed. Each reviewer must report its assigned dimension independently and assess actual evidence. Engine performs builds/tests/format checks/commits. Other concurrent tasks have separate file scopes; do not touch them.

briefs.implement: Phase implement. Make the frozen RED pass with minimal, clean production code inside the declared files and the approved scope. The frozen RED test must not change: when the RED itself is wrong, request a RED rework (request kind red-rework with its reason) instead; when the change needs files outside the declared files and approved scope, request a scope widen (kind scope-widen with the additional files and the reason) instead of editing them. An independent judge decides each request, approved files are carried forward as approved scope, and requests are capped. A task the spec declared no-red has no RED: make the change inside the declared files; the target's diff classifier refuses production code at commit. When test runs, comparisons, format results, reviews, oracle verdicts, QA runs, request decisions or reconciliation reports are bound, resolve every failure and blocking finding they report. Report changed files, hunks, a proof note, the test id and the RED test source (empty strings for a no-red task without a RED). acceptance: alpha() in alpha.go returns the int value 42.
alpha_test.go declares package sample and contains exactly one test function, TestAlpha(t *testing.T). It imports only "testing" and is gofmt-formatted (tabs, standard blank lines).
TestAlpha calls t.Fatal("got 0 want 42") when alpha() != 42.
Before the implement stage, TestAlpha compiles and fails on the current production code, and its output contains "got 0 want 42".
After the implement stage, TestAlpha passes and alpha_test.go is byte-for-byte the same as the frozen RED version.
No file other than alpha.go and alpha_test.go is modified, and no other function is added.
contracts: Signature stays unchanged: func alpha() int in package sample.
Test identity: TestAlpha in alpha_test.go is the only test with that name in the repository, and the engine runs it with -run '^TestAlpha$' ./...
Expected RED failure text: got 0 want 42
The RED test file is frozen after the test-first stage. The implement stage edits only alpha.go.
required_tests: TestAlpha (filter: -run '^TestAlpha$' ./...): proves that alpha() returns 42. It fails on the current code with "got 0 want 42" and passes once alpha() returns 42.
risks: The test must use the literal failure message "got 0 want 42" (not a formatted got/want) so the expected_failure check matches.
A duplicate TestAlpha name in another package would break the -run filter's uniqueness. The repository currently has no test files, so the risk is low.
Changing alpha_test.go during implementation would break the frozen RED. Only alpha.go may change then.
gofmt drift (for example spaces instead of tabs) in alpha.go or alpha_test.go would fail the format check.
fields.scope: Change alpha() in alpha.go (package sample) so it returns 42 instead of 0, and add exactly one RED unit test, TestAlpha, in a new file alpha_test.go. Only alpha.go and alpha_test.go change. beta.go, go.mod and every other file stay as they are. The change adds no new functions, dependencies or external effects.

findings.finding: The acceptance criterion "no other function is added" does not say that TestAlpha is excluded. TestAlpha is itself a new function. The criterion only makes sense if it means "beyond alpha() and the single TestAlpha". The other criteria and the scope make the intended reading clear, so this is unlikely to mislead the test-first or implement stage. Rewording it to "no function other than TestAlpha is added" would remove the ambiguity.

The spec does not say how TestAlpha calls alpha(). Because alpha is unexported, the test only compiles if it is in the same package (package sample, not sample_test). The spec does require package sample, so this is already covered. Stating it as the reason would make the requirement harder to misread.

The spec does not show the content of beta.go. The criteria assume beta.go does not already declare alpha or TestAlpha, and that the package compiles. alpha.go currently compiles as package sample, and the repository has no test files, so the uniqueness and RED-compile assumptions hold. This is a residual risk, not a defect.

Every criterion can be met and tested within the spec's own constraints. The RED test fails on the current code with exactly "got 0 want 42" because the current code returns 0, which matches the literal t.Fatal message. That expected failure text is substantive, not a bare got/want label, so it passes the RED report rules. The implement stage only needs to change alpha.go to return 42, which leaves the frozen test file untouched. The declared files, contracts and scope all agree with the operator's acceptance text, and the spec adds no extra scope.

Acceptance item 6 says 'no other function is added', but adding TestAlpha in alpha_test.go is itself a new function. Read in context, it means no new production or helper functions beyond TestAlpha. Clearer wording would be 'no function other than TestAlpha is added'. This doesn't block, because acceptance item 2 already caps alpha_test.go at exactly one test function.

The failure message is the fixed literal "got 0 want 42", so it would be misleading if alpha() ever returned a value other than 0 or 42. This is deliberate: the operator acceptance and the spec's risks require the literal message so the expected_failure match works. RED is checked against the current code, where alpha() returns 0, so the criterion can be met.

Every criterion can be met and tested within the declared scope. alpha.go holds 'func alpha() int { return 0 }' in package sample, so a test in package sample compiles and fails at run time with the required text. The repository has no other test files, so the name TestAlpha is unique under -run '^TestAlpha$' ./.... Changing the return to 42 needs edits to alpha.go only, so the frozen test file stays intact. declared_files matches the task_scope, and the scope adds nothing beyond the operator acceptance.

risks: The failure message must be the literal t.Fatal("got 0 want 42"). A formatted message such as t.Fatalf("got %d want 42", ...) could still produce the same text, but it breaks the acceptance wording and makes the expected_failure match depend on formatting.
If the test uses package sample_test, it cannot reach the unexported alpha(), so it fails to compile and the RED gate fails.
Any edit to alpha_test.go during the implement stage breaks the frozen RED. Only alpha.go may change then. If the RED itself is wrong, request a red-rework instead of editing the test.
gofmt drift, such as spaces instead of tabs or missing blank lines, in either file fails the format check.

beta.go's content was not shown. If it already declared alpha or TestAlpha, the package would fail to compile or the name would not be unique. alpha.go currently compiles and the repository has no test files, so the risk is low.
Acceptance item 6 ('no other function is added') should be read as 'no function other than TestAlpha'. Adding helpers or extra tests would violate it.
steps: Test-first stage: create alpha_test.go in package sample. It must be package sample, not sample_test, because alpha is unexported. Import only "testing" and declare exactly one function, `func TestAlpha(t *testing.T)`. Its body is `if alpha() != 42 { t.Fatal("got 0 want 42") }`. Format it with gofmt: tab indentation, a blank line after the package clause and a blank line after the import.

Test-first stage: set the RedReport's expected_failure to the literal "got 0 want 42", with the test name TestAlpha and test_file alpha_test.go. On the current code, alpha() returns 0, so the test compiles and fails at run time with that message.
Freeze alpha_test.go after RED. Do not edit it at any later stage.

Implement stage: in alpha.go, change only the return value, from `func alpha() int { return 0 }` to `func alpha() int { return 42 }`. Keep the signature, the package clause and the gofmt formatting. Add no other functions, imports or files.

The engine then runs `go test -run '^TestAlpha$' ./...`, which should pass, plus the gofmt check. It also confirms that alpha_test.go is byte-identical to the frozen RED version and that beta.go and go.mod are unchanged.
fields.test_placement: A new file, alpha_test.go, in the repository root next to alpha.go, in package sample (same-package white-box test, because alpha is unexported). It contains a single test, TestAlpha, which the engine selects with -run '^TestAlpha$' ./...

fields.proof: The frozen TestAlpha calls t.Fatal("got 0 want 42") only when alpha() != 42. alpha() now returns 42, so that branch is never taken and the test passes. The signature func alpha() int in package sample is unchanged, the gofmt formatting is preserved, and no functions, imports or files were added. alpha_test.go is untouched, so it is byte-identical to the frozen RED. The engine has not run the tests yet.

findings.finding: The test hardcodes the failure message "got 0 want 42". If alpha() ever returns a value other than 0 or 42, the message will report the wrong value. A formatted message such as t.Fatalf("got %d want 42", got) would be more accurate. The spec and RED contract require this literal string, so this is a note only and needs no change.

No security impact. Production now has a constant change in alpha.go (`return 0` becomes `return 42`), and the function signature is the same. Nothing handles input, I/O, networking, files, credentials, concurrency or new dependencies. The RED test imports only "testing", and its only side effect is t.Fatal with a fixed message. The change touches none of the sensitive domains (credentials, network-exposure, file-serving), so no organisation security guidance applied, and none was supplied in this dispatch.

Quality reviewer: the test hardcodes the failure message "got 0 want 42" instead of formatting the actual value (for example t.Fatalf("got %d want 42", got)). If alpha() returned some other wrong value, the message would be misleading.
findings.rationale: The observation is correct, but the spec, the risks list and the operator's acceptance all require this exact literal string so that the expected_failure match works. Changing it would break the contract. Keep it on record as a possible follow-up only.

findings.finding: Security reviewer: no security impact. The production change replaces one constant return value, and the test imports only "testing" and has no side effects beyond t.Fatal.
findings.rationale: Correct and informational. The diff only replaces `return 0` with `return 42`. There is no I/O, input handling, new dependency or sensitive domain, so nothing needs to be done.

fields.rationale: Every acceptance item is met. (1) alpha.go now has `func alpha() int { return 42 }` in package sample, with the signature unchanged. (2) alpha_test.go declares package sample, imports only "testing" and holds exactly one test, TestAlpha(t *testing.T). Both files are gofmt-clean: tabs are used, and gofmt accepts a one-line function body. (3) TestAlpha calls t.Fatal("got 0 want 42") when alpha() != 42. (4) Against the original production code (`return 0`), the test compiles and reaches that t.Fatal, so its output contains the expected text. The RED report from the test-first stage declared this failure, and the pipeline went on to implement, which means the RED gate accepted it. (5) The post-implementation EngineRun on tree a40bc70 shows a fresh build, 1 test matched and 1 executed, exit_code 0 and red_passed=true. The Compare stage reports the frozen RED as unchanged=true. (6) The implementation hunk changes only alpha.go, and no function, import or file was added. beta.go and go.mod are untouched. All four reviewers approved. The two reviewer findings are valid but non-blocking, and I found no blocking issue.

It keeps func beta() int unexported in package sample and in gofmt one-line form. The EngineRun on tree b18ec2c ran a fresh build, matched and executed 1 test, exited 0 and reported red_passed=true. That covers both the RED gate and GREEN. The Compare stage reports the frozen RED test as unchanged. The repository contains only alpha.go, beta.go, go.mod and the new beta_test.go, so TestBeta is unique and is the only test in the suite. The targeted GREEN run therefore also covers the full suite. All four reviewers approved. The three reviewer findings describe the same issue: the assertion message is hardcoded.
